title: Rate Limiting and Abuse Prevention
query: A user's agent is calling send_email 1000 times per minute. What's the BEST approach to prevent abuse while maintaining legitimate use?

options.text: Block the user completely after detecting high volume
Implement per-user, per-function rate limits with exponential backoff
Add CAPTCHA challenges for each function call
Tell the LLM to rate-limit itself through prompts

explanation: PER-USER, PER-FUNCTION RATE LIMITS (B) balance security and usability. Implementation: (1) Track calls per user per function in sliding window, (2) Set reasonable limits (e.g., 10 emails/min), (3) Return 429 error when exceeded with retry-after header, (4) Exponential backoff prevents thundering herd. Option A is too harsh (could be legitimate spike). Option C breaks UX. Option D is insecure (LLM can't enforce limits). Rate limits should be at execution layer with monitoring.
learning_points: Rate limiting prevents abuse while allowing legitimate use
Use sliding window algorithm for accurate rate tracking
Return 429 (Too Many Requests) with Retry-After header
Different functions need different limits (send_email: 10/min, search: 100/min)
Monitor for abuse patterns, not just volume
Implement exponential backoff in retry logic
abuse_detection: Unusual call patterns (midnight activity for normally daytime user)
Same function called with same parameters repeatedly
Geographic anomalies (calls from multiple countries simultaneously)
production_practices: Alert on sustained high-volume from single user
Implement circuit breakers for downstream services
Use distributed rate limiting (Redis, not in-memory)
Different limits for different user tiers (free vs paid)
Gradual limit increases for trusted users
